title: Arthur Schopenhauer's birth chart
metaDescription: Arthur Schopenhauer's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 3.5° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Five of the ten placements whose signs are settled fall in water signs — at least half of what the unknown hour leaves certain. Water reads the room before the room speaks — atmosphere first, analysis later.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 3.5° of Pisces is the Sun's exact seat — first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by Jupiter in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 12.2° Pisces; Venus stands at 3.6° Aries; Mars stands at 8.5° Cancer. The tradition reads thought steeped in tone and memory from Mercury, attraction declared rather than implied from Venus, effort that surges when it matters from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Jupiter and Pluto hold the closest angle here — a trine, 0.4° wide. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, the Sun conjunction Saturn at 1.9°, and Mercury trine Mars at 3.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Jupiter, Neptune, Pluto close a triangle of trines. A grand trine is read as self-sufficiency in one element: the current circulates whether or not anything is asked of it.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags four placements in this chart. Mercury in Pisces at 12.2° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Aries at 3.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Cancer at 8.5° is in fall; Jupiter in Gemini at 16.7° is in detriment. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives water 5, air 3, earth 1, fire 1, and mutable 5, cardinal 4, fixed 1 across the modes. Water weights a chart toward the felt and the remembered — information that arrives as atmosphere before it arrives as words. Uranus and Neptune were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Virgo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.4° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 15.7°.
